havamal:4:0.heard: Visit the friend you trust. Grass and brush grow over a path that no one walks. Give gifts, exchange thoughts, and answer warmth with warmth. The gift need not be splendid. A small present given in the right spirit can secure a welcome.

havamal:0:1.expected: Before crossing a threshold, look around. No one knows where an enemy may be sitting. But when a traveller comes to your own door, give him a fire for cold knees, food, dry clothing, water for washing, and a welcome that permits him to speak.
havamal:0:1.heard: Before crossing a threshold, look around. No one knows where an enemy may be sitting. But when a traveler comes to your own door, give him a fire for cold knees, food, dry clothing, water for washing, and a welcome that permits him to speak.

havamal:10:0.expected: I entered Suttungr's dwelling in search of the precious mead. Rati drilled a passage through stone. I risked my head among the giants. Gunnlöð gave me the drink and helped me escape. I repaid her badly. Where I had received aid, I left sorrow.
havamal:10:0.heard: I entered Satungra's dwelling in search of the precious mead. Rathi drilled a passage through stone. I risked my head among the giants. Gunload gave me the drink and helped me escape. I repaid her badly, where I had received aid I left sorrow.

havamal:2:0.expected: Watch before speaking. Listen to others without imagining that every smile proves friendship. Do not eat so greedily that your appetite becomes the room's entertainment. Drink with care: ale can steal judgement while seeming to offer pleasure.
havamal:2:0.heard: Watch before speaking. Listen to others without imagining that every smile proves friendship. Do not eat so greedily that your appetite becomes the room's entertainment. Drink with care. Ales can steal judgment while seeming to offer pleasure.

havamal:5:0.expected: Wealth does not establish wisdom. Do not mock another's poverty. The lame can ride, the handless can tend animals, and the deaf can fight. Living still offers possibilities that a funeral pyre cannot. The herds that fill a rich man's yard today may be gone tomorrow.
havamal:5:0.heard: Wealth does not establish wisdom. Do not mock another's poverty. The lame can ride, the handless contend animals and the deaf can fight. Living still offers possibilities that a funeral pyre cannot. The herds that fill a rich man's yard today may be gone tomorrow.

havamal:17:0.expected: I know songs that help in distress and songs that concern healing. I know how to blunt weapons, loosen fetters, and stop a flying shaft. I can quench a burning hall, reconcile enemies, and calm a dangerous sea. I can protect companions going into battle, and speak with a hanged man.
havamal:17:0.heard: I know songs that help in distress, and songs that concern healing. I know how to blunt weapons, loosen fetters, and stop a flying shaft. I can quench a burning hall, reconcile enemies, and calm a dangerous sea. I can protect companions going into battle, and speak with a hanged man.

havamal:9:0.expected: I found Billingr's woman resting in bed. She told me to return later, when our meeting could remain secret. Hope carried me away. When I returned at night, armed people and bright lights blocked my approach. At dawn I tried again, believing the household finally asleep. A dog lay tethered where I expected to find her.
havamal:9:0.heard: I found Billinger's woman resting in bed. She told me to return later, when our meeting could remain secret. Hope carried me away. When I returned at night, armed people in bright lights blocked my approach. At dawn I tried again, believing the household finally asleep. A dog lay tethered where I expected to find her.

havamal:12:1.expected: Loddfáfnir, do not let a wicked person determine your actions. Keep faith with a good friend. Do not take pleasure in another's misfortune. Beware desire for another man's wife, and the destructive words that pass between people. Do not ridicule an old speaker because his body has grown frail. Knowledge can remain where strength and beauty have gone.
havamal:12:1.heard: Lod Favnear, do not let a wicked person determine your actions. Keep faith with a good friend. Do not take pleasure in another's misfortune. Beware desire for another man's wife, and the destructive words that pass between people. Do not ridicule an old speaker, because his body has grown frail. Knowledge can remain where strength and beauty have gone.

voluspa:15:1.expected:
She sees rising
for a second time
earth from the sea,
ever green.
voluspa:15:1.heard: She sees rising for a second time earth from the sea evergreen.

voluspa:5:1.expected:
I know an ash standing,
called Yggdrasill,
a tall tree, sprinkled
with pale moisture.
voluspa:5:1.heard: I know an ash standing called Yggdrasil, a tall tree sprinkled with pale moisture.

voluspa:11:1.expected:
An axe-age, a sword-age,
shields are split;
a wind-age, a wolf-age,
before the world falls.
voluspa:11:1.heard: An axe age, a sword age, shields are split, a wind age, a wolf age before the world falls.

voluspa:7:0.expected: I know where you have hidden your eye, Odin, in Mímir's famous well. You came to me alone and offered rings and necklaces for knowledge. Would you know more?
voluspa:7:0.heard: I know where you have hidden your eye, Odin. In Mimir's famous well, you came to me alone and offered rings and necklaces for knowledge. Would you know more?

voluspa:12:1.expected: Surtr comes from the south carrying destructive fire, his sword shining like the sun. Rocks break, beings crowd the road to Hel, and the sky itself is torn apart.
voluspa:12:1.heard: Surtur comes from the south carrying destructive fire, his sword shining like the sun. Rocks break, beings crowd the road to hell, and the sky itself is torn apart.

voluspa:16:0.expected: A hall roofed with gold stands brighter than the sun, offering dwelling and happiness. But there comes Níðhöggr, the dark dragon, flying with corpses upon his wings. Now I must sink.
voluspa:16:0.heard: A hall roofed with gold stands brighter than the sun, offering dwelling and happiness. But there comes Nihigra, the dark dragon, flying with corpses upon his wings. Now I must sink.

voluspa:1:0.expected: I remember the giants who fostered me long ago, and nine worlds beneath the earth. In that first age there was no shore to stand on, no cool waves coming in, no heaven raised above a field of grass.
voluspa:1:0.heard: I remember the giants who fostered me long ago, and nine worlds beneath the earth. In that first age there was no shore to stand on, no cool waves coming in, no heaven raised above a field of grass.

voluspa:3:1.expected: Then three gods found Ask and Embla on the land. They had no settled destiny, no breath or understanding of their own. You gave them breath, Odin. Hœnir gave understanding, and Lóðurr gave warmth and good colour.
voluspa:3:1.heard: Then three gods found Ask and Embla on the land. They had no settled destiny, no breath or understanding of their own. You gave them breath, Odin. Honir gave understanding, and Lodur gave warmth and good color.

voluspa:4:0.expected: Above these beginnings stands the ash Yggdrasill, nourished by pale moisture, its dew falling into valleys. Beneath it are the women who determine lives. Urðr, Verðandi, and Skuld establish laws, choose lives, and set the fates of human beings.
voluspa:4:0.heard: Above these beginnings stands the ash-igdrasil, nourished by pale moisture, its dew falling into valleys. Beneath it are the women who determine lives. Urther verandhi and sculled established laws choose lives and set the fates of human beings.

voluspa:0:2.expected: Then listen, great and small, children of Heimdall. I remember a world older than your power, Odin. In my sight, what has happened and what must happen stand close together. You ask for knowledge. I will give it to you, but I promise no comfort.
voluspa:0:2.heard: Then listen, great and small, children of Heimdall. I remember a world older than your power, Odin. In my sight, what has happened and what must happen stand close together. You ask for knowledge. I will give it to you, but I promise no comfort.

voluspa:2:0.expected: At Iðavöllr they built high sanctuaries and halls. They established forges, made tongs, and worked metal. In the grass they played with golden gaming pieces, possessing gold without anxiety about its lack. Then three powerful giant women arrived.
voluspa:2:0.heard: At Aval they built high sanctuaries and halls. They established forges, made tongs, and worked metal. In the grass they played with golden gaming pieces, possessing gold without anxiety about its lack. Then three powerful giant women arrived.

voluspa:10:0.expected: A red cock crows among the giants. Gullinkambi wakes Odin's warriors, and another cock cries below the earth. Garmr howls before Gnipahellir. Bonds strain and break. Brothers kill brothers. Cousins destroy the obligations of kinship. Would you know more?
voluspa:10:0.heard: A red cock crows among the giants. Gullingkambi wakes Odin's warriors, and another cock cries below the earth. Garmor howls before a Nipahillier, bonds strain and break brothers kill brothers. Cousins destroy the obligations of kinship. Would you know more?

voluspa:12:0.expected: Heimdall raises the Gjallarhorn. You consult Mímir's head, Odin, while the old ash shakes and its branches tremble. Hrymr advances with his shield. The great serpent churns the sea. Naglfar is loose, and Loki comes with the force approaching over the water.
voluspa:12:0.heard: Heimdall raises the Gallerhorn. You consult Mimir's head Odin while the old ash shakes and its branches tremble. Hrimmer advances with his shield. The great serpent churns the sea. Naglfar is loose and Loki comes with the force approaching over the water.

voluspa:14:0.expected: Yet I see the earth rise again, green from the water. Waterfalls run. An eagle flies above them and catches fish beneath the cliffs. At Iðavöllr the gods who remain speak of the great serpent and remember the old powers. They find the golden gaming pieces in the grass.
voluspa:14:0.heard: Yet I see the earth rise again, green from the water. Waterfalls run, an eagle flies above them and catches fish beneath the cliffs. At Iteval the gods who remain speak of the great serpent and remember the old powers. They find the golden gaming pieces in the grass.

voluspa:13:0.expected: You meet the wolf, Odin, and you fall. Víðarr comes to avenge his father, driving his sword into the monster's heart. Freyr, the slayer of Beli, confronts Surtr. Thor kills the world-serpent, but victory does not save him. He takes nine steps before sinking beneath its venom.
voluspa:13:0.heard: You meet the wolf, Odin, and you fall. Vidar comes to avenge his father, driving his sword into the monster's heart. Freyr, the slayer of Belly, confronts Surtur. Thor kills the world serpent, but victory does not save him. He takes nine steps before sinking beneath its venom.

voluspa:8:0.expected: I see valkyries ready to ride. I see Baldr, your son, within the reach of death. A slender mistletoe shoot becomes the weapon Höðr will use. A brother born to avenge Baldr acts while scarcely a day old. He will not wash his hands or comb his hair before the killing is answered. Frigg weeps in Fensalir.
voluspa:8:0.heard: I see Valkyries ready to ride. I see Baldr, your son, within the reach of death. A slender mistletoe shoot becomes the weapon Hothr will use. A brother born to avenge Baldr axe while scarcely a day old. He will not wash his hands or comb his hair before the killing is answered. Frig weeps in Fensaldir.

voluspa:1:1.expected: Then the sons of Borr lifted the land and shaped the human dwelling of Midgard. Sunlight reached the stones from the south, and green growth covered the ground. Sun, moon, and stars did not yet know their places. The gods sat in council and named the divisions of time: morning, evening, and the reckoning of years.
voluspa:1:1.heard: Then the sons of Bohr lifted the land and shaped the human dwelling of Midgard. Sunlight reached the stones from the south and green growth covered the ground. Sun, moon and stars did not yet know their places. The gods sat in council and named the divisions of time, morning, evening and the reckoning of years.

voluspa:6:0.expected: I remember the first war. Gullveig was pierced with spears and burned in the High One's hall: three times burned, three times born, still living. Heiðr practised powerful magic. The gods debated responsibility and compensation. You cast a spear into the host, Odin. The defences of the Æsir broke, and the Vanir trod the field.
voluspa:6:0.heard: I remember the First War. Gullvague was pierced with spears and burned in the High One's Hall, three times burned, three times born still living. Haired practiced powerful magic. The gods debated responsibility and compensation. You cast a spear into the host Odin. The defenses of the Aesir broke, and the Vanir trod the field.

voluspa:9:0.expected: A bound figure resembling Loki lies with unhappy Sigyn beside him. Rivers run through poisoned valleys. Far from the sun stands a hall with doors facing north and walls woven with serpents. There I see oath-breakers and murderers enduring punishment. In Ironwood a giant woman breeds wolves. One of their kin will take the heavenly light.
voluspa:9:0.heard: A bound figure resembling Loki lies with unhappy Seagin beside him. Rivers run through poisoned valleys. Far from the sun stands a hall with doors facing north and walls woven with serpents. There I see oathbreakers and murderers enduring punishment. In Ironwood a giant woman breeds wolves. One of their kin will take the heavenly light.

vafthrudnismal:1:0.expected: Go safely, then, and return safely. May your mind be sharp in the exchange of words ahead.
vafthrudnismal:1:0.heard: Go safely then and return safely. May your mind be sharp in the exchange of words ahead.

vafthrudnismal:0:1.expected: I would rather keep you here among the gods. I know no giant equal to Vafþrúðnir in strength of understanding. This journey may end badly.
vafthrudnismal:0:1.heard: I would rather keep you here among the gods. I know no giant equal to Vafthrunir in strength of understanding. This journey may end badly.

vafthrudnismal:3:2.expected: And the horse that carries the night?
vafthrudnismal:3:2.heard: And the horse that carries the knight.

vafthrudnismal:2:1.expected: Come forward, then, and take a place to sit.
vafthrudnismal:2:1.heard: Come forward then and take a place to sit.

vafthrudnismal:4:2.expected: What is the field where Surtr and the gods will meet?
vafthrudnismal:4:2.heard: What is the field where Surtur and the gods will meet?

vafthrudnismal:4:0.expected: What river divides the gods' territory from the giants'?
vafthrudnismal:4:0.heard: What river divides the God's territory from the giants?

vafthrudnismal:3:0.expected: Tell me the name of the horse that brings day to humankind.
vafthrudnismal:3:0.heard: Tell me the name of the horse that brings day to humankind.

vafthrudnismal:6:1.expected:
We shall wager our heads
here in the hall,
guest, on our wisdom.
vafthrudnismal:6:1.heard: We shall wager our heads here in the hall, Guest on our wisdom.

vafthrudnismal:12:3.expected: I have travelled through the worlds, as far as Niflhel beneath the earth.
vafthrudnismal:12:3.heard: I have traveled through the worlds as far as Niflel beneath the earth.

vafthrudnismal:8:1.expected:
From Ymir’s flesh
the earth was fashioned,
and from his bones the mountains.
vafthrudnismal:8:1.heard: From Ymir's flesh the earth was fashioned and from his bones the mountains.

vafthrudnismal:17:1.heard: Now I have matched my wisdom in words with Odin. You are always the wisest of beings.

vafthrudnismal:14:1.expected: Víðarr and Váli will remain. Móði and Magni will possess Mjölnir after Thor has fallen.
vafthrudnismal:14:1.heard: Vidar and Vali will remain. Moe and Magni will possess Mjolnir after Thor has fallen.

vafthrudnismal:5:0.expected: You are learned, guest. Let us sit together and stake our heads on which of us is wiser.
vafthrudnismal:5:0.heard: You are learned guests. Let us sit together and stake our heads on which of us is wiser.

vafthrudnismal:14:3.expected: The wolf will kill the father of men. Víðarr will avenge him by tearing apart the monster's jaws.
vafthrudnismal:14:3.heard: The wolf will kill the father of men. Vidar will avenge him by tearing apart the monster's jaws.

vafthrudnismal:12:1.expected: They go out to fight each day. They strike one another down, then return restored to sit together.
vafthrudnismal:12:1.heard: They go out to fight each day, they strike one another down, then return restored to sit together.

vafthrudnismal:13:3.expected: Before her death she will bear a daughter. That daughter will follow her mother's path in the sky.
vafthrudnismal:13:3.heard: Before her death, she will bear a daughter. That daughter will follow her mother's path in the sky.

vafthrudnismal:10:1.expected: I remember Bergelmir, born long before the earth was made. I remember his being placed upon a lúðr.
vafthrudnismal:10:1.heard: I remember Bergelmere, born long before the earth was made. I remember his being placed upon a loother.

vafthrudnismal:1:3.expected: Who is this stranger speaking in my house? Unless you prove wiser than I am, you will not leave it alive.
vafthrudnismal:1:3.heard: Who is this stranger speaking in my house? Unless you prove wiser than I am, you will not leave it alive.

vafthrudnismal:11:1.expected: At the edge of heaven sits Hræsvelgr in the form of an eagle. The movement of his wings sends wind over the world.
vafthrudnismal:11:1.heard: At the edge of heaven sits Raysvelger in the form of an eagle. The movement of his wings sends wind over the world.

vafthrudnismal:16:2.expected: No one knows what you said in your son's ear. With a doomed mouth I have spoken ancient lore and the doom of the gods.
vafthrudnismal:16:2.heard: No one knows what you said in your son's ear. With the doomed mouth I have spoken ancient lore and the doom of the gods.

vafthrudnismal:5:2.expected: The earth was made from Ymir's flesh, the mountains from his bones, heaven from his skull, and the sea from his blood.
vafthrudnismal:5:2.heard: The earth was made from Ymir's flesh, the mountains from his bones, heaven from his skull, and the sea from his blood.

vafthrudnismal:13:1.expected: Líf and Lífþrasir will shelter in Hoddmímir's wood. Morning dew will sustain them, and human generations will descend from them.
vafthrudnismal:13:1.heard: Liff and Liffthrasir will shelter in Hodmimeir's wood. Mourning dew will sustain them, and human generations will descend from them.

vafthrudnismal:11:3.expected: He was made among the Vanir and given as a hostage to the gods. When the world reaches its end, he will return to his own people.
vafthrudnismal:11:3.heard: He was made among the Vanir and given as a hostage to the gods. When the world reaches its end, he will return to his own people.

vafthrudnismal:9:1.expected: Venomous drops came from Élivágar and grew into the first great being. Beneath his arm a man and woman grew. One foot begot a six-headed son with the other.
vafthrudnismal:9:1.heard: Venomous drops came from Elevagar and grew into the first great being. Beneath his arm a man and woman grew. One foot begot a six-headed son with the other.

vafthrudnismal:7:1.expected: Mundilfari is the father of the heavenly lights. Dellingr belongs to the account of day, Nörvi to that of night. Vindsvalr is winter's father, and Svásuðr is summer's.
vafthrudnismal:7:1.heard: Mandalfari is the father of the heavenly lights. Dellingar belongs to the account of day. Norvy to that of night. Vinsvalar is winter's father, and Svassurd is summer's.
